title: Single-Switch Basement Lighting with LED Retrofit

locations.name: Basement (probable)
locations.basis: Transcript repeatedly references basement as the setting for the mock-up and demonstration; no explicit shooting location is stated.

summary: This episode segment from This Old House demonstrates wiring a basement lighting circuit so that all fixtures (three basement lights with pull chains) are controlled by a single wall switch. The host walks through identifying the switch leg, reconfiguring the splice so power feeds all fixtures via one switch, and then upgrades the lighting with LED retrofit bulbs that fit the existing sockets with no extra wiring. After the changes, a test shows all lights come on together, the basement appears brighter, and a claim is made about reduced electricity usage and heat with the LED upgrade.
topics: White wire repurposed as hot (painted black)
Splice connections to feed multiple fixtures
No extra wiring for LED retrofit
Screw-in LED bulbs into existing sockets
